# Learning a Pfaffian-moment boundary law without reconstructing its bulk

2026-11-04. Status: scoped mathematical construction; independent review is recorded separately in AUDIT.md. No priority or transformative-consequence claim.

## 1. Contract

Let P be a probability distribution on k ordered spins x_i in {-1,+1}. Assume all odd moments vanish and every even moment obeys
E_P product_(i in S) x_i = Pf(C_S),
where C is the antisymmetric matrix with C_ij=E_P x_i x_j for i<j, and Pf(empty)=1. Call this the Pfaffian-moment promise. No unknown parameters beyond the pair correlations are supplied. We are given independent samples of all k spins in their correct boundary order.

A physical instance is the joint law of spins in cyclic order on a single face of a finite zero-field planar Ising network with free boundary conditions. In particular this includes ferromagnetic disk networks, with arbitrary hidden volume and arbitrary finite coupling magnitudes. This application uses the established boundary Pfaffian identity, not an asserted new Ising identity. A face-order promise is necessary; arbitrary interior spins, nonplanar networks, magnetic fields, or a weakly nonintegrable perturbation need not satisfy it. The proof below only uses the stated moment promise and positivity of P.

The operation produces an IMPROPER sampler: its learned law need not itself be a physical planar network or satisfy the Pfaffian-moment identity. With confidence at least 1-alpha over training data, its output distribution has TV distance at most epsilon from P. Training, stored representation, and per-output computation are polynomial in k, 1/epsilon and log(1/alpha), independent of the hidden bulk size and its inverse-problem condition number. This is not a certificate that arbitrary data satisfy the promise.

## 2. Fourier representation

For any antisymmetric matrix A, define a possibly signed mass function
p_A(x)=2^(-k) sum_(S even) Pf(A_S) product_(i in S) x_i.
Its total mass is one, its odd moments vanish, and its even moments are Pf(A_S), by Fourier orthogonality. Under the promise, p_C=P. Marginalization to an ordered subset I gives p_(A_I), regardless of whether p_A is nonnegative.

## Verdict and scope

The conditional learning theorem is mathematically supported. No counterexample or fatal gap was found in the derivative identity, uniform perturbation estimate, signed prefix formula, clipping argument, sample bound, or polynomial bit-runtime argument. The audit supplies independent derivations below rather than relying on the proposed proof's conclusions.

The initially supplied clipping bound was valid but unnecessarily loose. The stronger bound TV(Q,P)<=||q-P||_1/2 follows directly from domination and has been incorporated in the proof. The requested capped-coin clarification is now incorporated: probabilities zero and one are handled deterministically, and a positive-mass child is selected on a cap event. Neither the exact model promise nor novelty is certified by this review.

Reviewed final PROOF.md has SHA-256 35fff3eb5be9e986e33a01d7894d65392a597f2bb98c524d99f20ae3194d345d, including the capped-coin clarification and the exact evaluator for the capped law. Later substantive changes require separate review.

## 1. Derivative identity

Fix a matching M of r disjoint pairs and let U be its endpoints. In the defining Fourier polynomial, an upper-triangular variable A_ij occurs precisely in terms whose Pfaffian perfect matching includes edge (i,j). Differentiating with respect to all edges in M therefore deletes those weights and retains only such matchings.

The crossing parity of a retained matching splits into three parts: crossings within M, crossings within the residual matching, and crossings between those two matchings. For a fixed edge (i,j) and residual edge (l,h), the latter crossing indicator, modulo two, is

    1{i<l<j} + 1{i<h<j}.

Consequently all mixed crossing signs can be assigned independently to residual endpoints. Defining s_l=(-1)^(number of fixed edges enclosing l) and y_l=s_l x_l gives

    partial_M p_C(x)
      = sigma_M 2^(-2r) product_(i in U)x_i
          p_(C_(U complement))(y).

The normalization is 2^(-k)=2^(-2r)2^(-(k-2r)); there is no missing power of two. Removal of endpoints leaves the residual order unchanged. Crossing and nested fixed edges are both covered. Repeated differentiation in one edge, or differentiation in edges sharing an endpoint, gives zero.
